# Working at MCCS

## Benefits & Privileges

The employee benefits package is available to all regular full time and regular part time civilian Marine Corps nonappropriated fund (NAF) employees and includes the following for Regular Full Time and Part Time Positions:

- Medical and Dental
- Family Friendly Leave Program
- Life Insurance
- Flexible Spending Account
- Optional and Dependent Life Insurance
- Long Term Care
- 401(k) Savings Plan
- Short Term Disability
- Group Retirement Plan
- Leave (Sick & Vacation)

All MCCS Employees are encouraged to enjoy the use of our facilities and take advantage of a variety of employee benefits. (Facilities do vary from base to base.) Samples include:

- Marine Corps Exchange & Marine Marts
- Cabins & Lake Fishing
- Balance of Work & Family Life
- Lodging & Dining Clubs
- Libraries
- Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
- Childcare Facilities
- Auto Skills & Hobby Shop
- Paid Holidays
- Movie Theaters & Parks
- Discount Tickets and Leisure Travel Deals
- Recreational Equipment Rentals
- Swimming Pools & Fitness Centers
- Flexible Schedules
- Bowling Centers
- Training Opportunities

## Employee Training

Ethos is our Learning Management System (LMS). This system is accessible to all MCCS employees via the internet and allows ease in completing mandatory training as well as online learning opportunities for personal and professional development.

To begin from any internet browser, [click here.](https://usmc-mccs.csod.com/client/usmc-mccs/default.aspx)

- Once at the login page, you will enter your Username which is your "5-digit Employee ID Number" and your password which is the generic case-sensitive password "P4ssw0rd" (this is the number zero, not a letter).
- Click Accept & Login.

You will be prompted to change your password. Please change it to something that you will remember!

- Write it down and keep it somewhere safe!
- Once at the home page, look to the right of the screen to the cog icon. Hover your mouse pointer over the icon and choose the drop down My Account.
- Once there, look to the right and locate the Options drop down menu and click it.
- Choose edit security questions.
- You will be asked to provide your password again and then you need to answer the challenge questions.
- Once these are complete, if you forget your password, you will be able to reset your own password.

To begin from PeopleSoft login, [click here](https://hrms.usmc-mccs.org/landing/landing).

- Enter your UserID ("5-digit Employee ID Number"). At the next pop-up window, choose More Choices and select the "SIGNATURE" certificate. Enter your numeric CAC PIN.
- Once at the home page, choose the MCCS Training Ethos icon. You will be redirected another screen – choose the first option – "Check here if you are logging in on the MCCS.org network." NOTE: If you choose the "Click here if you are logging in externally (from home, .mil, etc.) you will need your user ID and password to access the site
- Once at the home page, look to the right of the screen to the cog icon. Hover your mouse pointer over the icon and choose the drop down My Account.
- Once there, look to the right and locate the Options drop down menu and click it.
- Choose edit security questions.
- You will be asked to provide your password and then you need to answer the challenge questions.
- Once these are complete, if you forget your password, you will be able to reset your own password.

To complete your Mandated Compliance Training:

Once at the Welcome page scroll down to the blue, square icons and choose My Learning.
Listed there you should see the training that needs to be completed.
To the right of the training title, you will see the 'Action' column. To begin or continue training, click the Launch button.
This will allow you to begin and/or complete the selected training. NOTE: If it does not launch in a new window, check to see if you have pop-up windows blocked. Make sure you set your default for this site to allow popup windows.
If you need to leave the training, the program will remember the last section that you completed and direct you there the next time you login to complete it.

## Consolidated Master Labor Agreement

All MCCS employees are protected by the Consolidated Master Labor Agreement between the United States Marine Corps and the American Federation of Government Employees.

pages.text:
# Catering/Special Events

The Clubs at Quantico & Crossroads Events Center will create a custom, worry-free event that will exceed your expectations. We offer premium banquet and reception space located on historic Marine Corps Base Quantico Virginia. Our professional and experienced staff offers unparalleled service ensuring no detail is overlooked.

The Clubs at Quantico and Crossroads Events Center offers a state of the art facility that can accommodate PME's, Dining In or Mess Night, Promotion or Retirement, Seminars, Conferences, Symposiums, Change of Command, and Weddings.

## Amenities

### Ballrooms

* PowerPoint presentations in 1 or all rooms including the Waller Room and Runners Room
* Video viewing to include watching video clips and DVDs
* Live projection of your guest speaker
* Wired or wireless lapel/handheld mics
* WIFI access
* Display active webpages on the projection screen
* DISH Network - Coming in the future
* XM Radio
* Inputs in the front and back of each ballroom for S-Video, Composite Video, Component Video, and VGA video, as well as sound input via a headphone jack

### Waller Room and Runner's Room

* 60" PLASMA MONITOR, 1080P
* PowerPoint presentations
* Video viewing

## Equipment

### Projection System

* 4 - Christie Digital LX-505 Projector with Christie Digital Zoom Lens 3.4-5.4:1 Zoom (1 per ballroom), 5K Lumens with a 1000:1 contrast ratio
* 4 - Motorized projection screen, wall mounted 78" x 104" SD format(1 per ballroom)
* Projectors and screens can be used in combination with adjacent rooms for larger size groups to allow for better sound/visual coverage of the material

### Sound System

* 24 - 5.25" High Power Coaxial Open-Ceiling Speakers (6 per ballroom)
* 1 - 4-Channel 200Watt/channel Professional Power Amplifier
* 4 - Nexia TC digital signal processor (1 per ballroom)
* 2 - Wireless lavalier microphones
* 2 - Wireless handheld microphones
* 4 - Wired handheld microphones

pages.title: Information, Tickets, and Tours
pages.text:
# Information, Tickets, and Tours

## Tickets

MCCS Rec/ITT program offers information and brochures about many local, regional and destination attractions. The staff searches out hot spots suitable for individual and family outings and tours of special interest to their customers. Rec/ITT offers discount tickets to many attractions: Kings Dominion, Busch Gardens, Six Flags America, Colonial Williamsburg, Walt Disney World, Universal Studios, Hershey Park, Luray Caverns, Medieval Times and much more. Contact the Rec/ITT office at 703-432-8850 for the latest ticket information and schedules or download the latest price list.

Recreation, Information, Tickets and Tours (Rec/ITT) is located inside the Quantico MCX, Building 3500, Russell Road. They offer information and discounts for local and regional attractions (i.e., theme parks, theaters, sporting events, etc.) to all authorized Patrons. (Ticket prices are subject to change without notice).

**Authorized Patrons:** Active Duty, Retired, Reserve Military, Coast Guard Personnel and Family Members. Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) on active duty. DoD Civilians, Full-time Quantico DoD Contractors, FBI/DEA Permanent Personnel and Students assigned to Quantico. Purple Heart recipients, former prisoners of war, or veterans with VA-documented service-connected disability ratings of 0-100% who have been issued a Veteran Health Identification Card (VHIC) from VA. Primary family caregivers of veterans must present an eligibility letter from the VA's Office of Community Care.

**Refund Policy:** All sales are final. No refunds or exchanges.

**National Parks Pass:** America owes a debt to those who make sacrifices to protect our country. To say "Thank You", Active Duty U.S. Military and their Dependents can pick-up a FREE Annual Pass to the National Parks and Federal Recreational Lands. [Click here](https://www.nps.gov/planyourvisit/veterans-and-gold-star-families-free-access.htm) to find out more details, or stop by the Rec/ITT Office.

**Disclaimer:** Rec/ITT is not affiliated with ITT Corporation, ITT Industries, or their subsidiaries.

## American Forces Travel

An MWR joint service initiative has resulted in the first official DoD online vacation travel site, American Forces Travel! With Priceline Partner Network® as the service provider, the site offers travel deals and benefits exclusively for Military members and authorized patrons! American Forces Travel provides access to a wide selection of discounted rates on hotels, air fare, rental cars, vacation packages, cruises and much more! pages.title: C Suites at Quantico
pages.text:
# C Suites at Quantico

The C Suites at Quantico is the best kept secret at MCB Quantico! Tucked away between the hills and tree you will find peace and sanctuary from the hustle and bustle of Quantico. This historic building offers an AirBnB style option while staying on base.

## Location

The C Suites at Quantico is located on the main side of Marine Corp Base Quantico. It is just up the road from the great Potomac River! The base is just 35 miles South of our national's capitol, Washington D.C. while Fredericksburg is just South of us. The base does have an Amtrak and VRE station for easy and convivence!

**24/7 Reservations: (888) 409-STAY(7829)**

## Suites

Our suites are more of a home styled apartment for you to stay in. Our suites are a 2 queen bedroom, 1 bath apartment that comes with a formal sunroom, formal living room, formal dining room, designated desk space with hard line ethernet, and fully equipped kitchen.

We are an AirBnB styled Recreational Lodging Facility. We are designed for independent travel. There's no front desk and no formal check-in or check-out — you'll receive your access details before arrival and can come and go at your convenience. Our team is available by phone if you need anything, but the experience is completely self-service for your privacy and ease. Each unit has an assigned parking spot right in front with additional guest parking spots. Housekeeping comes through daily Monday – Friday to provide clean linens, towels, take out trash, and do basic cleaning. There are 3 large TVs throughout the apartment- each one comes with cable and 2 are smart TVs for Netflix or Hulu. We also offer free on-site laundry, portable wifi pucks, privacy, and quietness, and on call staff.

Please note that our building is not wheelchair accessible and does require you to be able to walk upstairs. If this is a concern for you, please let me know and I can refer you to another lodging option. Our building is a smoke free building. We only have one (1) designated pet room. Please let me know if need this room and I can see if it is available.

The C Suites at Quantico is classified as a recreational lodging, therefore per diem do not apply to our facility. We do not charge any additional fees such as taxes or additional hotel fees. If you are staying with your pets, we will send you the additional required documents and payments. We do require a card on file, however for our longer-term guests we arrange a payment schedule that works best for you. This could be weekly, biweekly, or paying for a full month.

### Amenities:

- Self-check-in with key code
- No front desk — enjoy total independence
- Hotel-quality comfort with Airbnb-style flexibility
- Contactless stay — easy arrival, easy departure
- Assigned Parking Space
- On site Laundry Facility
- Complimentary Wi Fi and Cable
- Fully equipped kitchen with: fridge, freezer, microwave, stove, pots & pans, coffee maker, plates, bowls, cups, and silverware.
- Bedrooms: queen beds, walk in closets, alarm clocks, portable fans, and a tv
- Sunroom: couch, chairs, and tv
- Formal Dining Room: table that can set up to 6
- Living room: couch, tables, chair, and tv

## Cancellations

You can make changes or cancellations on your reservation up to 24 hours before your reservation at no penalty.

All changes to reservations must go through our 24/7 Reservation Hotline at 1-888-409-7829. Once the modification has changed, you will receive a new confirmation email.

Cancellations or changes to a reservation made any less than 24 hours prior to check in will result in the loss of one night stay ($139.00)

## Payment

We accept all major credit cards.

At time of booking, payment must be made in full. Reservations are not considered confirmed until payment has been paid in full.

## Eligibility

Anyone who has access to base is eligible to stay with us at the C Suites at Quantico. Reservations are accepted for all eligible personnel on a first come first serve basis. Reservations and room assignment are made without regards to rank, grade, or time of reservation.

Please know that since this is a historic building from the early 1900s, there are no elevators or ADA access to this building. Stairs are required to get into the building.

Reservation for MCB Quantico Recreation Lodging does not guarantee access to the base. Please make sure to verify all policies/restrictions prior to arrival. They may vary based on the installation and/or location. This may affect (but not limited to) certain guest eligibility such as DOD Civilians, contractors, retired civilians, sponsors, foreign nations, etc.

For more eligibility information, please visit the MCB Quantico Visitor's center page at [Base Access](https://www.quantico.marines.mil/Info/Base-Access/).

## Policies

We do not offer early check ins or late check outs. Check in is at 4pm. Check out is at 11am. If you stay past the check-out time, you will be charged a late fee of one night ($139.00)

We do provide a full equipped kitchen, you must bring your own food items such as coffee, filters, condiments, and other food items.

Our housekeepers are only able conduct light cleaning around the apartment. Our housekeepers are not able to touch personal items, do dishes, or move personal items. If you would like your bed made, please make sure your personal items are off the bed. If you would like your floors vacuumed and cleaned, please make sure your personal items are off the floor.

Any unauthorized animals found inside the unit will be charged $350 and asked to leave without a refund for their stay.

Please not that during your stay, the building might not be available for safety and security reasons without notice. All individuals will have to leave the building immediately. In those events, the MCCS team will notify you and provide alternative lodging options and refund any funds from that point.

Mail is not able to be delivered to this building. There is a US Post Office located down the hill in the Town of Quantico to set up any mailing needs. There is also an Amazon pick up station located at the Marine Mart on Barnett Ave.

## Pets

MCCS Recreational Lodging offers one (1) pet friendly room. To reserve this room, you may call the 24/7 Reservation number or book online and select the Pet Friendly Room.

No other rooms are allowed to have any animals in their rooms. If a nonauthorized animal is found in your room, a fee of $350 will be applied to your account and you will be asked to leave without a refund of your stay.

If staying in our pet friendly room, A non-refundable pet fee will be charged automatically to the guest's account upon check-in based upon the length of stay:
- 1 night: $30
- 2-6 nights: $65
- 7-30 nights: $125
- An additional charge of $50 for every 7 nights after initial 30 nights

## Next Steps

Once you have booked your stay either through the 24/7 call center or through our online reservation system, you should receive an automatic email with your confirmation information.

You have until 24 hours before check-in to cancel or modify your reservation without penalties

3 days before your check-in date, you will receive an email with instructions about your remote check-in process and directions with how to get to our location.

At 3:30pm on day of your check-in, you will receive another email with your code, directions to our location, and our check-in process. Please note, checking in before 3:30pm is not possible at this location.

## Contact Information and Resources

### C Suites at Quantico Information

Lejeune Rd
Quantico, VA 22134

**24/7 Reservations:** (888) 409-STAY(7829)

[Book Now](https://lodgingreservations.usmc-mccs.org/Search/Index/17735/90/)

pages.text:
# Child and Youth

Child and Youth Programs (CYP) provides affordable, high-quality childcare to children 6 weeks to 12 years of age. The goal is to provide a safe and nurturing environment that promotes the physical, social, emotional, cognitive, and language development of children enrolled in the programs. Services are provided in Child Development Centers, School-Age Care Program, and Family Child Care homes. All programs are designed to assist Active Duty (AD) and Department of Defense (DoD) personnel in balancing the competing demands of family life, accomplishing the mission, and improving the economic viability of the family unit.

## Child Development Centers

(CDCs) serve children 6 weeks thru 5 years of age (prekindergarten). Curriculum goals and plans are based on regular, documented observations and assessments of each child's level of development, strengths and interests while respecting family values. Lesson plans are posted in each child's classroom and are readily available on-site for parents to see. Both CDCs are accredited through the National Association for the Education of Young Children (NAEYC). The program is center-based, child initiated, and teacher supported, with an emphasis on active participation through individual and small group learning experiences.

Environmental accommodations, materials, and equipment are adjusted to support and maximize learning opportunities. CDC classroom staff offer activity centers/learning areas that allow children the opportunity to explore, create, imagine, and experience their environment. Staff is readily available to facilitate learning and provide nurturing encouragement to each child. Each activity is designed with a goal that promotes further development and prepares your child for the next level of learning.

## Resource and Referral

The Resource and Referral (R&R) Office provides childcare information, referrals, and assistance in locating appropriate, affordable, and accessible childcare for military personnel and DoD employees. R&R can provide resources for community-based childcare. An R&R representative is located at CDC South, 703.784.0674/4453.

**The USDA and Quantico MCCS are equal opportunity providers and employers.**

Related Resources:
- [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/)
- [Child Development Center (CDC)](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/child-development-centers)
- [School-Age Care (SAC) Program](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-age-care)

## Family Child Care

Family Child Care (FCC) providers are military spouses that are licensed by the Base Commander to care for children in government quarters. They complete the same program training as center-based care givers. Homes are inspected regularly and complete ongoing training monthly. FCC Providers offer activity centers/learning areas that allow children the opportunity to explore, create, imagine, and experience their environment. Providers are readily available to facilitate learning and provide nurturing encouragement to each child. Each activity is designed with a goal that promotes further development and prepares your child for the next level of learning.

**FCC Director** – 703.784.2011

**Extended Hours:** Extended hours are from 0500-0600 and 1800-1900 and are available when reserved one week in advance for Active Duty patrons only. The cost is the hourly care rate per child.

**Special Events Care:** Units aboard MCB Quantico may request childcare services for special events. Contact CYP Administration office for more information, 703.784.3760.

**Parent Orientation:** Families receive a welcome orientation specific to their child's program. This is the opportunity for parents to share information about their child to help ensure a positive start. The orientation covers policy and instructions to help make your family's transition to CYP smooth. It is necessary and mandatory to attend an orientation prior to your child's start date.

pages.text:
# Child Development Centers

We foster physical, cognitive, social, and emotional development in a safe and nurturing environment for children ages 6 weeks to 5 years.

---

## Getting Started Is Easy

### How to Get Started

Families seeking child care are required to submit their requests through [Military Child Care](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome).

To initiate a request, families must first create an account with MilitaryChildCare.com, log in, and complete their household profile using the steps outlined in the link below.

[Create an Account](https://www.mcccentral.com/training-center/components/family-user-account-and-household-profile#801)

### Forms

The following forms are required for registering for child care:

* [Child and Youth Programs Health Assessment](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=3490d39d-a951-4831-a364-dc3078f2b734&v=1)
* [Child and Youth Programs Registration Form](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=a20869e0-cd7e-423a-93d3-ef5fbbe59786&v=1)
* [CYP Non-Medicated Topical Products Form](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=3a6d9279-f207-4d0e-9400-1245c683da9e&v=1)
* [Application for Department of Defense Childcare Fees](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=20990cf2-e066-429b-b1f1-8de9b1782731&v=1)

---

## Child Care Resources

### Full-time Child Care

**Curriculum:**

All Child Development Centers use the Early Learning Matters (ELM) curriculum as the primary classroom curriculum. ELM is based on the latest research on child development and best practices in early education and care. ELM offers a comprehensive, developmentally appropriate approach to meaningful learning for all children featuring:

* A whole child focus on skills that bolster school readiness and life success.
* Developmentally sequenced activities that embed strategies for individualizing learning.
* Evidence-informed, friendly-to-use resources for classroom staff and families.

At the heart of the ELM curriculum are activity plans that build on children's pathways of development in five infant/toddler areas and eight preschool areas.

**Accreditation & Certification:**

CDCs are required to be nationally accredited and must pass an annual Department of Defense inspection to obtain a certificate to operate.

### School Age Care

School Age Care (SAC) offers vital support to military families. To enroll your children into SAC, visit [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/).

**Key Benefits:**

* **Safe and Structured Environment** - Provides a secure, supervised setting for children ages 5-12
* **Academic Support** - Offers homework assistance, tutoring, and educational activities
* **Social Development** - Encourages children to build friendships and develop teamwork
* **Resilience Building** - Promotes emotional well-being and adaptability through programs that help children manage unique challenges of military life
* **Recreational Activities** - Provides engaging, age-appropriate activities that promote physical fitness and creativity
* **Support for Military Readiness** - Enables military parents to focus on their mission
* **Affordable and Flexible Care Options** - Offers cost-effective programs with flexible care schedules
* **Connection to MCCS Resources** - Provides access to other MCCS programs, such as Family Advocacy, Youth Sports, and the Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP)

### Hourly Child Care

Hourly child care may be available on your installation Child Development Centers (CDC) for an hourly rate per child.

* Hourly child care does not require parents to make a request on [militarychildcare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/).
* Parents need to complete and submit the CDC packet and provide the necessary supporting documents to register their child.
* This service is provided based on space availability or may not be offered at your installation.
* Contact your local installation's CDC for availability.

---

## Family Support Resources

### PCS Workshop

The Permanent Change of Station (PCS) Workshop is designed to guide Marines and their families through every step of the relocation process.

Nine reasons to attend a PCS Workshop:

1. **Policy** - Per MCO 1754.10B, attending the PCS Workshop is required for a smooth transition to your new duty station.
2. **Installation-specific Information and Contacts** - Get valuable information about your new installation, including key contacts and local services.
3. **Household Goods Weight Allowances & Entitlements** - Learn about your weight allowances for household goods and what entitlements you can access during your move.
4. **Travel Allowances, Budget, and Government Card** - Understand your travel allowances, how to budget for the move, and how to use your government travel card.
5. **Moving with Pets** - Receive guidance on transporting pets, quarantine regulations, and other related requirements.
6. **School Liaison & Exceptional Family Member Program Resources** - Access support for school enrollment and resources for family members with special needs.
7. **Spouse Employment Opportunities** - Discover job search assistance and career development resources for spouses.
8. **Personalized Relocation Plan & Online Relocation Resources** - Create a customized relocation plan and explore online resources to streamline your move.
9. **Sponsorship** - As per MCO 1320.11H, learn how to request a sponsor to help you adjust and settle into your new duty station.

Don't move alone. Contact your [Information, Referral, and Relocation](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/information-referral-and-relocation) specialist for PCS Workshop information.

### School Liaison

The School Liaison is a vital resource for Marines and their families new to an installation, helping to ensure a seamless transition for children into local schools.

School Liaison support includes:

* **School Enrollment** - Guidance on enrolling children in local schools and understanding registration requirements.
* **Local School Information** - Up-to-date resources about school districts, programs, and options available in the area.
* **Home School Information** - Assisting families with guidance on registering with the DoDEA schools.
* **Exceptional Family Member Support** - Help with navigating the special education process and accessing available services.
* **Transition Assistance** - Resources for families moving to a new area, including information on school calendars and schedules.

For more information about support and services, visit the [School Liaison](https://yuma.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-liaison) webpage on the MCCS website.

### Exceptional Family Member Program

The Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP) is essential for service members and their families with special needs, providing support and resources to ensure a smooth transition to a new installation.

EFMP Services Available Include:

* **Enrollment Assistance** - Guidance on enrolling in the EFMP and understanding program requirements.
* **Specialized Support Services** - Access to resources for medical, educational, and emotional support tailored to family members with special needs.
* **Transition Assistance** - Help with relocating to a new area, including information on local schools, medical facilities, and community services.
* **Advocacy and Resources** - Connection to advocacy services and local support groups to assist families in accessing necessary care and benefits.
* **Workshops and Training** - Opportunities for families to participate in workshops focused on managing special needs and navigating available resources.

Learn more about how EFMP supports you and your family by visiting [EFMP](https://usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/exceptional-family-member-program).

### Marine Corps Family Team Building

Eligibility for participation in the Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB) programs extend to individuals across various segments of the military community:

* Active Duty Service Members: Including all branches of the military, all ranks.
* Department of Defense (DoD) Employees
* Spouses of Military Personnel

**How to get started with MCFTB:**

1. **Identify Individual Needs** - Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require.
2. **Connect with MCFTB** - Reach out to MCFTB professionals either in person or by phone.
3. **Attend Workshops and Classes** - Participate in MCFTB workshops, classes, and events relevant to your situation.
4. **Connect with Other Families** - Take advantage of opportunities to connect with other Marine Corps families through MCFTB-sponsored events, support groups, and social media platforms.

### New Parent Support

New Parent Support offers guidance, education, and support to our Marines, their families throughout our military community.

**Eligible Participants:**

* Parents with children up to age 5
* DoD Spouses
* DoD Families

Connect with your New Parent Support office to begin your journey with our caring professionals.

### Information, Referral, and Relocation

**Key Services Provided:**

* **Welcome Aboard Brief** - Provides newcomers with essential information about their new installation, local community, and available resources.
* **Relocation Assistance** - Offers one-on-one support for PCS moves, including help with planning, moving tips, and checklists.
* **Requesting a Sponsor** - Connects Marines and their families with trained sponsors to provide personalized support and guidance during relocation.
* **Lending Locker** - Supplies temporary household items, such as kitchenware and small appliances.
* **Base Housing Support** - Offers guidance on housing options, including on-base housing, rental listings, and off-base accommodations.
* **DEERS and ID Card Assistance** - Provides information and support for enrolling in the Defense Enrollment Eligibility Reporting System (DEERS) and obtaining necessary ID cards.
* **Child Care and School Liaison Support** - Helps families find child care and connects them with School Liaison Officers for school registration and educational resources.
* **Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP) Support** - Ensures families with special needs have access to tailored relocation assistance and resources at their new duty station.

**Benefits of IR&R Services:**

* Reduces stress and uncertainty associated with frequent moves.
* Enhances readiness by ensuring families are well-informed and prepared.
* Strengthens connections within the Marine Corps community.
* Provides access to resources that promote resilience and stability.

---

## Life Skill-building Resources

### Budgeting for Child Care

The professionals at [Personal Financial Management](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/personal-financial-management) can help you prepare for financial changes by offering guidance on budgeting, saving, and managing child care expenses.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

### What ages does the Child Development Center serve?

The Child Development Center provides child care to children from 6 weeks to 5 years old.

### How do I enroll my child in the Child Development Centers?

Enrollment is completed through [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/), where you can create an account, select your preferences, and join the waitlist.

Fees are based on total family income and follow the Department of Defense fee structure.

### What types of activities does the Child Development Center offer?

The Child Development Center provides age-appropriate activities that promote cognitive, social, emotional, and physical development through a structured curriculum.

### Who should I contact if I have additional questions?

You can contact the Child Development Center office at your installation for further assistance.

pages.text:
# Family Child Care

We provide your child, aged 6 weeks to 12 years, with a nurturing environment that supports their development and helps them thrive within the community.

---

## Getting Started is Easy

Navigating steps to successfully register for child care.

### Registration Guidance

Welcome to Family Child Care (FCC), where your child will learn, grow, and thrive in a safe and supportive environment. FCC Providers are highly trained and regulated, including thorough background checks and monthly inspections. FCC providers create a sense of belonging for families and support them in developing their child(ren)'s positive self-worth.

**Registration Steps:**

1. **Go to** [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/)
   - Set up an account if you don't already have one.
   - Add your child's information and request care at your installation.

2. **Join the Waitlist**
   - If space is not immediately available, your child will be placed on a waitlist.
   - You will receive an offer via email to inform you when a spot opens up.
   - If you are placed on a waitlist you have the option of contacting [MCCYN](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome/mccyn) which provides fee assistance to offset the costs of community-based care.

3. **Accept the Offer**
   - Once you receive an offer, follow the instructions to accept it within the given timeframe.
   - If you don't respond within the timeframe, the offer is removed, but you may request reactivation with supporting details if eligible.

4. **Complete the Registration Process**
   - After accepting the offer, you will receive forms to complete.
   - Provide necessary documents, such as proof of eligibility, immunization records, and emergency contacts.

5. **Attend Parent Orientation**
   - You will be required to attend an orientation to review program policies and expectations.

6. **Start Care**
   - Once all paperwork is submitted and fees are processed, your child can begin attending the program.

If you need help getting started please contact our Resource and Referral office.

### Eligibility

**Family Child Care is available to children of:**

- Active-duty Service Members
- DoD Civilian Employees
- Reservists
- DoD contractors

**Children:**
- Must be between the ages of 6 weeks to 12 years old.

**Enrollment:**
- Enrollment is guided by DoD priorities. Supplanting does not apply to FCC. To secure a spot, families are encouraged to register early, as availability may vary depending on demand.

**Department of Defense Policies:**
- [DoDI 6060.02](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=c8ad90d5-2d16-44a7-95b6-224de21dfd54&v=1)
- [MCO 1710.30A](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/modules/media/?do=download&id=a98aa33f-1d48-4466-8530-c790d725bfed&v=1)

For more information on eligibility, priority placement, and registration requirements, please contact our Resource and Referral office.

### MilitaryChildCare.com

MilitaryChildCare.com makes it easy to find and request Family Child Care (FCC), giving you peace of mind knowing your child is in a safe and supportive environment.

With just one online account, you can explore program options, submit a request, and manage your childcare needs from anywhere. Spaces are assigned based on DoD priority placement, so registering early ensures you have the best chance of securing care when you need it.

Start today by visiting [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome).

---

## Child Care Support

### I Need Child Care

**Flexible, Home-Based Child Care for Your Family**

Family Child Care (FCC) offers a safe, nurturing, and home-like environment for children ages 6 weeks to 12 years. With small group sizes and flexible hours, FCC provides personalized care that fits your family's schedule, including full-time, part-time, evening, and weekend options. Licensed providers are trained to support your child's development while ensuring a warm, engaging atmosphere.

**Eligibility & Requirements:**

Family Child Care (FCC) is designed to support military families by providing high-quality, home-based child care. Eligibility is based on priority and availability.

- Active-Duty Service Members
- Department of Defense (DoD) Civilians
- Reservists & National Guard Members
- Retirees
- DoD Contractors

**Age Requirements**
- Children must be between 6 weeks and 12 years old to enroll in FCC.
- School-age children (up to 12 years) may attend before/after school care, full-day care during school breaks, and summer programs.

**Health & Immunization Requirements**
- All children must have up-to-date immunization records, including age-appropriate vaccines as required by DoD and state regulations.

**Special Needs & Accommodations**
- The CYP behavior specialist, CYP nurse, and FCC providers work together to assess and accommodate children with special needs.
- Parents must disclose any medical, developmental, or dietary requirements during registration to ensure proper care and support.

If you have any question please contact our Resource and Referral office.

### I Want to Provide Child Care

As a Family Child Care provider, you'll offer safe, high-quality care for military children while enjoying flexible hours, professional training, and the ability to care for your own children at home. MCCS provides free training, support, and resources to help you succeed.

**Why Become an FCC Provider?**

- Run your own home-based business while supporting military families.
- Enjoy flexible hours and the ability to care for your own children at home.
- Receive training and support at no cost, including CPR, First Aid, and child development courses.
- Gain access to resources and equipment, including a lending library of toys and materials.
- Participate in the USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program to receive meal reimbursements.

**Eligibility Requirements:**

- Must be at least 18 years old.
- Have a high school diploma or equivalent.
- Reside in government housing or approved off-base housing.
- Pass a comprehensive background check for all household members over 18.
- Complete a health screening for yourself and any family members who will be in the home.

**Steps to Get Started:**

1. Contact your local Family Child Care office to learn more about the application process and training requirements.
2. Download and complete the FCC Application or obtain it from the Resource and Referral office. Application requires background checks.
3. Complete a family interview (provider applicant and spouse)
4. If interested in processing with the certification process, background checks are initiated.
5. Pay a non-refundable $50 training fee at Family Child Care office which covers the cost of the CPR/First Aid training. *Training fees are not required at all locations. Contact the Resource and Referral office about training fees.*
6. Attend FCC Provider initial training - 40-hours (one-week)
7. Complete health requirements for all household members
8. Set up home in accordance with regulatory requirements.
9. Home inspection by Fire, Safety & Sanitation.
10. Quality Review Board.
11. Documentation sent to SJA regarding successfully completion of requirements (to obtain authorization to operate a home business).
12. (Upon SJA approval) Provider files Housing Addendum, notifying Family Housing of FCC business
13. Purchase Liability Insurance.
14. Upon clearance to start, Resource & Referral will assist in setting up provider's profile on [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/)
15. Final walk-through by FCC staff.
16. Open for business!
17. Be committed to attending ongoing training sessions to guarantee the highest quality of care for children. This includes monthly evening training.

Homes should obtain certification from the command if they provide more than 10 "child care hours" per week. For instance, if a resident looks after two children for five hours, it amounts to 10 hours of child care. Homes that operate outside this framework without certification will be deemed unauthorized. Enforcement against such unauthorized care will be as per the Housing Office rules and regulations. Detailed information can be found on page 6 of the Resident handbook.

The FCC program is not only about providing care but also about ensuring that the caregivers are well-trained, certified, and provide a safe and nurturing environment for the children. The command plays an active role in monitoring and certifying providers, ensuring the best care for the children enrolled in the FCC program.

If you have any questions please contact our Resource and Referral office.

---

## Life Skill-building Resources

### School Liaison

The School Liaison is a vital resource for Marines and their families new to an installation, helping to ensure a seamless transition for children into local schools. By providing essential information and support, the School Liaison assists families in navigating educational options and addressing any concerns related to their child's education.

**School Liaison support include:**

- **School Enrollment** - Guidance on enrolling children in local schools and understanding registration requirements.
- **Local School Information** - Up-to-date resources about school districts, programs, and options available in the area.
- **Home School Information** - Assisting families with guidance on their local school district homeschool requirements.
- **Special Education Support** - Help with navigating the special education process and accessing available services to include warm hand offs to EFMP.
- **Transition Assistance** - Resources for families moving to a new area, including information on school calendars and schedules.

For more information about support and services, visit the [School Liaison](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-liaison) webpage on the MCCS website.

### Exceptional Family Member Program

The Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP) is essential for service members and their families with special needs, providing support and resources to ensure a smooth transition to a new installation.

EFMP helps families navigate the challenges associated with relocating by connecting them to specialized services and community resources tailored to their unique circumstances.

**EFMP Services Available Include:**

- **Enrollment Assistance** - Guidance on enrolling in the EFMP and understanding program requirements.
- **Specialized Support Services** - Access to resources for medical, educational, and emotional support tailored to family members with special needs.
- **Transition Assistance** - Help with relocating to a new area, including information on local schools, medical facilities, and community services.
- **Advocacy and Resources** - Connection to advocacy services and local support groups to assist families in accessing necessary care and benefits.
- **Workshops and Training** - Opportunities for families to participate in workshops focused on managing special needs and navigating available resources.

Learn more about how EFMP supports you and your family by visiting [EFMP](https://usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/exceptional-family-member-program).

### Budgeting Your Child Care

The professionals at [Personal Financial Management](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/personal-financial-management) can help you prepare for financial changes by offering guidance on budgeting, saving, and managing educational expenses.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

- Blended Retirement System (BRS)
- Car Buying
- Consumer Awareness
- Continuation Pay
- Couple Financial Counseling
- Credit Report and Credit Score Analysis Saving and Investing
- Credit / Debt Management
- Developing a Spending Plan
- Financial Education Action Points (FEAP)
- Individual Financial Counseling
- Major Purchases
- Military Pay & Benefits
- Retirement Planning
- Survivor Benefits Plan
- Thrift Savings Plan
- Understanding Military Retirement Benefits

### Marine Corps Family Team Building

[Marine Corps Family Team Building](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/marine-corps-family-team-building) (MCFTB) is designed to enhance the resilience, readiness, and well-being of all members of the Marine Corps community, including service members, spouses, children, extended family members, command leaders, units, and support personnel.

**How to get started with MCFTB:**

- **Identify Individual Needs** - Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require. MCFTB offers a variety of workshops, classes, and resources tailored to different needs, including deployment support, spouse education and career assistance, relationship-enhancement, and more. MCFTB professionals can help you identify your specific needs.

- **Connect with MCFTB** - Reach out to MCFTB professionals either in person or by phone. They can provide guidance on available programs, workshops, and resources that best suit your needs.

- **Attend Workshops and Classes** - Participate in MCFTB workshops, classes, and events relevant to your situation. These could include pre-deployment briefs, relationship-enhancement classes, pre-marital and marital workshops, relocation assistance workshops, family readiness seminars, financial planning classes, and more.

- **Connect with Other Families** - Take advantage of opportunities to connect with other Marine Corps families through MCFTB-sponsored events, support groups, and social media platforms. Building connections with other families can provide valuable support and camaraderie.

### Libraries

The [Library](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/libraries) is a great resource for families and school-age children, offering books, educational programs, and activities that support learning and growth. Whether you're looking for homework help, fun storytimes, or a quiet place to read and explore, the Library provides a welcoming space for children to develop their love of learning.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

- **Children's Collection:** A diverse selection of picture books, chapter books, movies, and audiobooks designed for young readers.
- **Summer Reading Program:** Featuring free activities and incentives to encourage a love of reading during the summer months.
- **Storytime Kits:** Themed kits that include books and activities, allowing families to enjoy storytime at their convenience.
- **Educational Programs and Activities:** Various events and workshops that enrich your children's learning experiences.
- **Access to Digital Resources:** Online materials, including e-books and educational databases, to support learning and exploration. Visit the [DoD MWR Virtual Library](https://marines.dodmwrlibraries.org/).

### Guiding Growth & Resilience

[Community Counseling](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling) provides support to ease this transition by offering emotional support, stress management strategies, and adjustment counseling. Counselors help families navigate the challenges of relocation, offering guidance on coping with change, building resilience, and connecting with local resources.

Through individual and family counseling, the program helps create a smooth transition, strengthening the overall well-being of military families.

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

- Relationship Concerns
- Work Stressors
- Life Stressors
- Trauma
- EAS/PCS and Challenges Related to Transition
- Grief and Loss
- Sadness
- Worry
- Deployment Cycle Stressors and Reintegration
- Adjustment
- Crisis Intervention
- Sleep Hygiene
- Parent-Child Communication

---

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**Q: Who can become a Family Child Care provider?**
A: Any military spouse or eligible individual 18 years or older who lives in base housing or approved off-base housing can apply. Providers must complete training, background checks, and home inspections to become licensed.

**Q: What are the benefits of becoming an FCC provider?**
A: FCC providers run their own home-based business, set their own hours, care for their own children while earning income, receive free training and resources, and participate in the USDA Child and Adult Care Food Program.

**Q: What are the requirements for enrolling a child in FCC?**
A: Children must be between 6 weeks and 12 years old, have up-to-date immunizations, and meet health and safety requirements. Families must register through MilitaryChildCare.com or their local Resource & Referral (R&R) office.

**Q: How is Family Child Care different from a Child Development Center (CDC)?**
A: FCC provides home-based care in smaller groups, offering more personalized attention, flexible hours, and a family-like setting compared to larger Child Development Centers (CDCs).

**Q: How do I find an FCC provider for my child?**
A: Parents can search for available FCC providers and request care through MilitaryChildCare.com or contact their local FCC office or Resource & Referral (R&R) office for assistance.

---

# New Parent Support

The New Parent Support Program (NPSP) is a voluntary strength-based parent education program which is delivered through education and support, parent support groups, and the ability to link parents to appropriate referrals and resources. Program eligibility is offered to all service members, family members who are expectant parents, and parents of children from birth to five years of age.

Even if you have been raising your family for a few years, challenges may arise as your child grows and develops. The NPSP offers you the opportunity to express your concerns, ask questions, enhance parent child relationships and parenting techniques, build skills, set goals, and gain new knowledge. Please contact us for more information at (703) 784-4248.

## Programs

**Baby Boot Camp**

Learn how to make the time you have with your baby as stress-free and enjoyable as possible. Learn coping skills to decrease anxiety of first time parenting. Learn the basics of newborn care. Learn how to calm a fussy baby and reduce the risk of Shaken Baby Syndrome.

**Pregnancy 101**

Explore pregnancy, labor, and delivery. Gaining knowledge and asking questions early can reduce stress and support your pregnancy journey.

**Mothers In Formation**

Mothers In Formation is a supportive space for active duty moms to connect, share experiences, and build community. This monthly group offers encouragement, stress-management tools, and discussion around balancing military life and motherhood. Join us to connect with other moms, strengthen support networks, and focus on your well-being.

**Post-Partum Support International**

The purpose of the organization is to increase awareness among public and professional communities about the emotional changes that women experience during pregnancy and postpartum. Approximately 15% of all women will experience postpartum depression following the birth of a child. Up to 10% will experience depression or anxiety during pregnancy. When the mental health of the mother is compromised, it affects the entire family.

https://www.postpartum.net/

**Breastfeeding Basics**

Class Focus: Breastfeeding

## Home Visitation

**What is Home Visitation?**

The New Parent Support Program Home Visitors are Licensed Clinicians, Licensed Social Workers and/or Licensed Marriage Family Therapists. The purpose of home visits is to provide individualized parenting education and support to parents of young children up to age six and to help parents increase their parenting skills so that they are successful parenting their children throughout each stage of development. Home visits take place in the family's home. The frequency of the visits range from once a week to once a month depending on your family's needs and interests.

Home Visitors provide education on a variety of topics to include, but not limited to: age appropriate discipline, developmental screenings, managing sibling rivalry, effective communication with your children, stress management, toilet training, nutrition, Sudden Infant Death Syndrome and deployment issues.

Some people receive parenting education, while others request support and encouragement regarding the challenges of parenting.

Call (703) 784-4248 to register.

# School Age Care

We offer a safe, engaging environment for children ages 5-12, providing homework assistance, recreational activities, and social development opportunities to support their growth and well-being.

**Phone:** 703-784-2249

**Address:** 3312 Purvis Rd, Quantico, VA 22134

**Hours:**
- Monday: 6:00am - 6:00pm
- Tuesday: 6:00am - 6:00pm
- Wednesday: 6:00am - 6:00pm
- Thursday: 6:00am - 6:00pm
- Friday: 6:00am - 6:00pm
- Closed on weekends and federal holidays

## Getting Started is Easy

### Registration Guidance

Welcome to School Age Care (SAC), where your child will learn, grow, and thrive in a safe and supportive environment. Through engaging activities, meaningful connections, and opportunities to build essential life skills, SAC supports children to develop confidence, resilience, and a sense of belonging. We're excited to be part of their journey!

Registration is quick and easy—simply follow the steps below.

1. **Go to** [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://militarychildcare.com/).
   - Set up an account if you don't already have one.
   - Add your child's information and request care at your installation.
2. **Join the Waitlist**
   - If space is not immediately available, your child will be placed on a waitlist.
   - You will receive an offer when a spot opens up.
   - If you are placed on a waitlist you have the option of contacting MCCYN which provides fee assistance to offset the costs of community-based care.
3. **Accept the Offer**
   - Once you receive an offer, follow the instructions to accept it within the given timeframe.
   - If you don't respond within the timeframe, the offer is removed, but you may request reactivation with supporting details if eligible.
4. **Complete the Registration Process**
   - After accepting the offer, you will receive forms to complete.
   - Provide necessary documents, such as proof of eligibility, Flu shot records, and emergency contacts.
5. **Attend Parent Orientation**
   - You may be required to attend an orientation to review program policies and expectations.
6. **Start Care**
   - Once all paperwork is submitted and fees are processed, your child can begin attending the program.

If you need help, contact the Resource and Referral office. They can answer questions and guide you through the process.

### Eligibility

School Age Care (SAC) is designed to provide a safe, enriching environment for children while supporting the unique needs of military families. We proudly serve those who serve by offering quality care that fosters learning, resilience, and connection.

**School Age Care is available to children of:**
- Active-duty Service Members
- DoD Civilian Employees
- Reservists
- DoD contractors.

**Children:**
- Must be between the ages of 5 and 12 years old
- Enrolled in Kindergarten through 6th grade to participate in the program.

**Enrollment:**
- Enrollment is guided by DoD priorities. To secure a spot, families are encouraged to register early, as availability may vary depending on demand.

**Department of Defense Policies:**
- DoDI 6060.02
- MCO 1710.30A

For more information on eligibility, priority placement, and registration requirements, contact the Resource and Referral office.

### MilitaryChildCare.com

MilitaryChildCare.com makes it easy to find and request School Age Care (SAC), giving you peace of mind knowing your child is in a safe and supportive environment. With just one online account, you can explore program options, submit a request, and manage your childcare needs from anywhere. Spaces are offered based on DoD priority placement.

## School Age Care Support

### Curriculum Focus

Our curriculum is built around key focus areas: Character & Leadership Development; Education & Career Development; Health & Life Skills; The Arts; Sports, Fitness & Recreation; Technology. Our program follows nationally recognized standards and is affiliated with the Boys & Girls Clubs of America (BGCA).

### Meals Provided

- **Before & After School Care:** A nutritious breakfast and an afternoon snack are provided.
- **Early Release / Teacher Workdays / School Breaks:** Breakfast, lunch, and an afternoon snack are included.

**Special Dietary Needs:** Inform School Age Care staff of any food allergies or dietary requirements during registration. We will work with you to accommodate where possible.

Our meals follow USDA nutritional guidelines. Meals offered can vary by location, check with the School Age Care center for details.

### Transportation

- **On-Base Schools:** Transportation is typically provided for children attending schools located on the installation.
- **Off-Base Schools:** Availability of transportation for off-base schools varies by location. Please check with your local center for details.
- **Field Trips & Special Activities:** During school breaks and summer camp, supervised transportation is provided for planned excursions and enrichment activities.

**Parent Responsibilities:** If your child attends a school that is not part of the SAC transportation service, you will need to arrange their drop-off and pick-up.

Not all installations provide transportation. For more information on transportation options at your location, contact the Resource and Referral office.

### Youth Connections

Youth Connections is designed to help children adjust, make friends, and feel comfortable in their new community. When a new child joins the program, they are paired with a friendly and experienced SAC ambassador—a peer who helps them navigate their new environment.

### Parent Orientation

Parent Orientation provides important information about program policies, daily routines, and what to expect: program policies and expectations (pick-up and drop-off procedures, behavior expectations, communication with staff), safety and emergency procedures, meals and nutrition, meeting SAC staff, and completing required paperwork. If you have any questions or need to schedule your orientation, please contact the Resource and Referral office.

### Supporting Children with Special Needs

**How to Request Accommodations**
- During the registration process, inform SAC staff that your child has special needs.
- Complete required Child & Youth documentations.
- Provide relevant documentation or recommendations from medical providers, or therapists if applicable.
- Work with SAC staff to develop a support plan that best supports your child's needs.

If your child has special needs and you have questions about accommodations, contact the Resource and Referral office.

### Seasonal Camps

Seasonal camps provide a safe, engaging environment where children ages 5-12 can explore new interests, build friendships, and develop essential life skills. View the upcoming camps listed in our calendar or contact the Resource and Referral office.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**Who is eligible for School Age Care?** Children ages 5-12 who are enrolled in kindergarten through 6th grade are eligible.

**How do I register my child for care?** Register online at MilitaryChildCare.com and follow the steps to request care.

**Is there a waitlist for School Age Care?** Yes, if no spots are available, your child will be placed on a waitlist, and you will be notified when a spot opens.

**What are the program hours?** Hours vary by location but typically include before and after school care, full-day care on school breaks, and summer camp.

**Does School Age Care provide meals?** Breakfast and snacks are provided on school days; lunch may be required on certain days, such as teacher workdays or school breaks.

## Contact Information

**School-Age Care** — 3312 Purvis Rd, Quantico, VA 22134 — Phone: 703-784-2249 — Monday–Friday 6:00am - 6:00pm; closed on weekends and federal holidays.

# School Liaison

We support military families by prioritizing the educational needs of their children, providing resources, and ensuring smooth transitions between schools.

## Connect with a School Liaison

Getting connected is easy.

### Eligibility

Members of our military community with school-aged children (PreK-12) are eligible to access the services provided by the School Liaison Program.

- Active-duty Service Members
- DoD Civilian
- National Guard
- Reserves
- Retirees

### Getting Started

Figuring out schools during a move or facing school-related questions can be tough, but you don't have to do it alone. Your School Liaison is here to help make things smoother for you and your family.

**Contact the School Liaison**  
Reach out to your local School Liaison office for personalized support.

**Schedule a Consultation**  
Set up a meeting or phone call with the School Liaison to discuss your child's needs, school options, and any concerns you may have regarding the transition.

**Collect Important Documents**  
Maintain important records, such as school transcripts, report cards, individual education plans (IEPs), and any other documentation that will assist the School Liaison in supporting your family.

**Learn About Local School Options**  
The School Liaison can provide details on the local school districts, private schools, charter schools, homeschooling, and other alternative education options to help you make an informed decision.

**Explore Available Resources**  
The School Liaison can direct you to resources such as tutoring services, scholarships, extracurricular activities, and other programs.

**Stay Connected**  
Maintain communication with the School Liaison throughout your assignment to receive ongoing support and updates on educational opportunities for your child.

Don't hesitate to contact your School Liaison, who is ready to support your family's educational journey!

### School Liaisons

School Liaison Officers help to navigate the challenges of school transitions, ensuring access to quality education, and providing valuable support for your children's academic success.

### Our Support

Learn how the School Liaison can support you and your family.

The School Liaison will provide you with important information, assist with enrollment, navigate grade and credit transfers, and ensure that your child receives support to connect to their new environment. The School Liaison can also help you facilitate communication with principals, teachers, or other school staff, making your child's transition smoother.

Empowering you with the information you need, they ensure you can make informed decisions about your child's education and be their strongest advocate.

Your School Liaison is the critical link between families, commands, communities, and schools.

- Promotes and enhances education services and programs.
- Provides incoming families with information regarding Local Education Agencies.
- Leverage the Interstate Compact and assist with grade/credit transferability.
- Ensure children/youth and LEAs are supported by military community.
- Facilitate command sponsored Adopt-a-School opportunities.

## Resources for Military Families

Additional services to strengthen and support military families.

### Adjusting to Changes

Moving to a new duty station can be challenging for military families, especially for children adjusting to a new school and environment.

[Community Counseling](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling) provides support to ease this transition by offering emotional support, stress management strategies, and adjustment counseling. Counselors help families navigate the challenges of relocation, offering guidance on coping with change, building resilience, and connecting with local resources.

Through individual and family counseling, the program helps create a smooth transition, strengthening the overall well-being of military families.

Life Skills Development Resources:

- Relationship Concerns
- Work Stressors
- Life Stressors
- Trauma
- EAS/PCS and Challenges Related to Transition
- Grief and Loss
- Sadness
- Worry
- Deployment Cycle Stressors and Reintegration
- Adjustment
- Crisis Intervention
- Sleep Hygiene
- Parent-Child Communication

### Budgeting for Your Move

[Personal Financial Management](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/personal-financial-management) is here to support your military family during your move to another duty station. From budgeting for relocation expenses to understanding allowances, and managing housing costs, our experts provide guidance to help you stay financially secure throughout your transition. Connect with us to plan ahead and make your move easier!

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

- Blended Retirement System (BRS)
- Car Buying
- Consumer Awareness
- Continuation Pay
- Couple Financial Counseling
- Credit Report and Credit Score Analysis Saving and Investing
- Credit / Debt Management
- Developing a Spending Plan
- Financial Education Action Points (FEAP)
- Individual Financial Counseling
- Major Purchases
- Military Pay & Benefits
- Retirement Planning
- Survivor Benefits Plan
- Thrift Savings Plan
- Understanding Military Retirement Benefits

### Libraries

The [Library](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/libraries) is a great resource for families and school-age children, offering books, educational programs, and activities that support learning and growth. Whether you're looking for homework help, fun storytimes, or a quiet place to read and explore, the Library provides a welcoming space for children to develop their love of learning. Stop by and discover all the ways we support your family!

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

- **Children's Collection:** A diverse selection of picture books, chapter books, movies, and audiobooks designed for young readers.
- **Summer Reading Program:** Featuring free activities and incentives to encourage a love of reading during the summer months.
- **Storytime Kits:** Themed kits that include books and activities, allowing families to enjoy storytime at their convenience.
- **Educational Programs and Activities:** Various events and workshops that enrich your children's learning experiences.
- **Access to Digital Resources:** Online materials, including e-books and educational databases, to support learning and exploration. Visit the [DoD MWR Virtual Library](https://marines.dodmwrlibraries.org/).

### Before & After School Care

[School Age Care](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-age-care) (SAC) programs support your military family with after-school care, learning opportunities in a safe environment. Whether you need care before or after school, help with homework, or a nurturing home environment for your child, these programs provide safe and reliable options.

**School Age Care (SAC)**  
SAC offers child care for kids in kindergarten through age 12, giving them a structured and fun environment when they're not in school. You can rely on SAC for:

- **After-School Support** – Your child will have a safe place to go before and after school, during holidays, and over the summer. They'll enjoy fun activities, make friends, and stay active while you focus on your work or military duties.
- **Educational Services** – SAC provides homework help, tutoring, and learning activities that support what your child is doing in school.
- **Support for Military Families** – If your schedule changes due to training or deployment, SAC offers flexible hours so your child always has consistent care.

Register for School Age Care at [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome#/).

### Exceptional Family Members

The [Exceptional Family Member Program](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/exceptional-family-member-program) (EFMP) is dedicated to supporting military families by ensuring they have access to the resources and services needed to thrive. We understand that navigating military life with a family member who has special needs can be challenging, which is why EFMP works closely with the School Liaison Program to provide seamless support for educational transitions, school advocacy, and special education resources. Together, we help families find the best-fit schools, understand their rights, and access individualized services that promote academic success and overall well-being.

How EFMP Supports Families:

- **Lending Library** – Borrow sensory tools, assistive devices, and educational materials to support learning and development at home.
- **Respite Care Services** – Provides temporary relief for caregivers, ensuring they have time to recharge while their loved one receives quality care.
- **Assignment Coordination** – Ensures that families are stationed at locations with appropriate medical and educational services for their exceptional family members.
- **Advocacy & Support** – Assists families in navigating the special education system, including IEPs (Individualized Education Programs).
- **Workshops & Resources** – Offers educational sessions on topics like navigating the EFMP process, advocacy skills, and community resources.

By working together, EFMP and the School Liaison help ensure that your child receives the support they need—at home, in school, and throughout their military journey. We are here to support you every step of the way!

### Family Child Care

[Family Child Care](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/family-child-care) (FCC) gives you in-home child care from trained and certified providers, often military spouses, in military housing. This program is great if you prefer a smaller, home-like setting for your child. FCC offers:

- **Home-Based Care** – Your child will be cared for in a safe, nurturing home setting with small group sizes and personalized attention.
- **Educational Activities** – FCC providers include age-appropriate learning, playtime, and rest in their daily schedules, helping your child grow and develop.
- **Flexible Child Care** – Whether you need full-time, part-time, or overnight care, FCC providers can work with your schedule, making it easier to handle deployments or unpredictable work hours.

### Information, Referral, and Relocation

Moving to a new duty station can be overwhelming, but you don't have to navigate it alone. [Information, Referral, and Relocation](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/information-referral-and-relocation) (IR&R) services are here to help you and your family transition smoothly and feel at home in your new community.

**Here's how IR&R can support you:**

- **Relocation Assistance** – Get guidance on housing, base services, child care, and community resources to establish stability for your family.
- **Local School Information** – Connect you to the School Liaison, educational resources, enrollment requirements, and district policies to ensure a smooth school transition.
- **Welcome Aboard Resources** – Access newcomer checklists, area guides, and personalized referrals to help you get familiar with your new surroundings.
- **Lending Locker** – Borrow temporary household items to make settling in easier while you wait for your belongings to arrive.

Wherever your journey takes you, IR&R is here to provide the information and resources you need to make your transition as smooth as possible.

### Marine Corps Family Team Building

[Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/marine-corps-family-team-building) is designed to enhance the resilience, readiness, and well-being of all members of the Marine Corps community, including service members, spouses, children, extended family members, command leaders, units, and support personnel.

How to get started with MCFTB:

1. Identify Individual Needs: Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require. MCFTB offers a variety of workshops, classes, and resources tailored to different needs, including deployment support, spouse education and career assistance, relationship-enhancement, and more. MCFTB professionals can help you identify your specific needs.

2. Connect with MCFTB: Reach out to MCFTB professionals either in person or by phone. They can provide guidance on available programs, workshops, and resources that best suit your needs.

3. Attend Workshops and Classes: Participate in MCFTB workshops, classes, and events relevant to your situation. These could include pre-deployment briefs, relationship-enhancement classes, pre-marital and marital workshops, relocation assistance workshops, family readiness seminars, financial planning classes, and more.

4. Connect with Other Families: Take advantage of opportunities to connect with other Marine Corps families through MCFTB-sponsored events, support groups, and social media platforms. Building connections with other families can provide valuable support and camaraderie.

## FAQs

### What does the School Liaison do?

The program helps military families navigate the education system and assists with school transitions, special education services, and local school information.

### Who can use the School Liaison?

The program is available to active-duty military families, National Guard and Reserve members on active orders, DoD civilians, and retired service members with school-aged children, whether families live on or off base.

### How can the School Liaison help during a PCS move?

School Liaisons provide resources for enrolling in new schools, transferring credits, and ensuring a smooth transition. They can also help find information on local schools, extracurricular activities, and educational support.

### What educational resources are available through the School Liaison?

School Liaisons provide access to resources such as tutoring, special education information, and connections to homeschooling or virtual school options.

### Can the School Liaison assist with special education needs?

Yes, School Liaisons can help families understand the special education process, connect with local resources, and support children with IEPs (Individualized Education Programs) or 504 Plans.

### Can School Liaisons help with college readiness?

Yes, School Liaisons provide resources for college planning, scholarships, and navigating the college admissions process.

### Do School Liaisons only work with DoDEA schools?

No, School Liaisons support families regardless of whether their children attend public, private, DoDEA schools, or homeschool families. They are knowledgeable about all education options available in the local area.

# Information, Referral, and Relocation

## Welcome Aboard

Helping you navigate relocation and connect to your community.

### Welcome Aboard Brief

Welcome to your new installation! The Welcome Aboard Brief is designed to provide key information and resources to ensure a smooth transition for you and your families. During this brief, you will receive important updates on life at the base and how to access resources and services.

Topics discussed will include:

* Base Services and Amenities
  Overview of essential services, such as medical facilities, commissary, exchange, and fitness centers.

* Relocation Assistance
  Guidance on housing, transportation, and accessing resources through the Relocation Assistance Program (RAP).

* Childcare and School Information
  Details on childcare options, school enrollment, and youth programs to support your family.

* Sponsorship and Family Readiness
  Introduction to the Sponsorship Program and Family Readiness Officers (FRO) for ongoing support and connection to your new community.

* Local Area Orientation
  Information on local attractions, shopping, dining, and community activities to help you settle in and explore your new surroundings.

View the event calendar for scheduled Welcome Aboard Briefs or reach out to the Information, Referral, and Relocation office for availability and registration.

### Your MCCS Connection

Welcome to the MCCS Enterprise Website!
Looking for comprehensive resources and support for service members and their families? The MCCS Enterprise Website is your hub for programs, services, and tools designed to enhance your quality of life, support mission readiness, and strengthen your community.

Discover:

* Career and Education Resources
* Family Support Services
* Fitness, Recreation, and Leisure Programs
* Financial Management Tools
* And much more!

Explore [MCCS](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/) now.
